evidence: Current source reads, edits and manual review only. No builds, tests, syntax checks, project/game/JNI/shader/GPU execution, process inspection, native commands or exports. Runtime parity remains unverified by user instruction.
problem: An export cleanup previously sent an unconditional resume. Export step/sample and playback rate changes also checked acknowledged ownership after applying their operation. A current-state report alone cannot prevent a queued command from changing a replacement clock before that mismatch is detected.

contract.field: Optional expectedClock object on the existing schema-1 clock request. Fields: session, sequence, requestId (string or explicitly absent identity), freezeSequence, frozen, playbackRate (finite f32 0..16 or null). Frozen and rate modes are mutually exclusive. No C export or engine ABI change.
contract.idle: An idle expectation permits only freeze/rate acquisition and requires no active lease/pending acknowledgement, real step, world tick or rate application. Sequence zero requires no last acknowledgement and a null request identity. A nonzero idle sequence must match its last acknowledgement, including a known null request ID from a legacy manual command; missing metadata is not guessed into a new identity.
contract.active: Held/rate follow-ups require the same current session, acknowledgement sequence/request ID, freeze generation, frozen mode and exact f32 rate bits. A live lease and no outstanding acknowledgement/timer/world/rate work are required. A held expectation cannot acquire a replacement freeze.
contract.checks: Native command admission and the actual selected simulation-timer consumer both compare expectedClock under the native clock state lock before accepting the incoming transition. Ordinary operation/session/sequence/timer validations remain in place. Unrelated existing timer maintenance and independent lease expiry continue normally.
contract.acknowledgement: Accepted native receipts echo the applied expectedClock. The core worker requires that exact echo with its existing correlated request/op/completion checks. Guard mismatch at deferred application goes to requestRejected, preserving the current owner's last acknowledgement, lease and pending state instead of replacing them with a rejected request's receipt.
contract.compatibility: Unchanged explicit/manual clock_control requests may omit the optional guard and retain their prior behavior. Updated replay/export coordinators always send guards; they do not retry without them. Older native readers rejecting this new field are unsupported for these guarded paths. This is state coordination, not a security boundary or proof of native rendering.

core.acquire: clock_control_from_idle validates the observed root clock identity/capability and encodes that expectation. Export binding retains its idle snapshot for initial freeze; playback acquisition reobserves the same idle sequence after helper correlation. Native admission/application rechecks make a stale report insufficient to acquire another controller's clock.
core.followup: clock_control_owned derives a bounded active expectation from a successful acknowledged receipt. NativeExportClock uses it for step/sample; PlaybackClock uses it for rate changes and renewals. Initial acquisition is handled separately.
core.release: resume_owned_clock derives the same active expectation. Export success/error cleanup, its pre-controller freeze fallback and playback release use this guarded operation. Changed ownership is an error; there is no unconditional recovery resume.
core.alreadyIdle: For resume only, a bounded recent report may confirm that the same sequence/request/freeze identity is already idle with no lease/queued/pending/rate work or restoration failure. Return that actual status with releaseSkipped=owned_clock_already_idle. No command is published and no acknowledgement is synthesized. This observation does not promise that another controller cannot acquire afterward.
core.idempotence: NativeExportClock caches a successful clock release or same-identity idle observation without publishing another command or consuming another sequence. Its direct-camera ownership cleanup now has a separate acknowledgement/cache (replay-camera-ownership-source.json); clock release is attempted independently of camera failure. A failed clock release remains failed and the native lease remains the independent fallback.
core.budgets: Existing 4 KiB native request and bounded clock-report admission remain. The expectation contains only one prior identity, not a recursively nested receipt history. Command publication uses the existing unique request ID and atomic local file path.

remaining: Build and installed-game validation of guarded idle acquisition, follow-up/cleanup races, deferred rejection, exact acknowledgement echo, real-timer restoration, lease expiry and world replacement.

Recovery of commands whose acknowledgement was lost after possible application. The last known owner may no longer match; cleanup must report uncertainty and let native expiry act rather than release an unowned replacement state.
Atomic helper/native speed transitions, exact epoch alignment and scheduling drift. Guarded ownership does not prove shared replay time or native simulation/terrain/animation fidelity.
